Hand-drawn illustration of three people comparing three model cards, representing a roundup of alternatives to the Kimi K3.1 Pro AI model

TL;DR

The closest Kimi K3.1 Pro alternative is Claude Sonnet 5.5: same $2/$10 per million tokens, about three times the output speed, and a near-identical benchmark score. Gemini 4 Argon also sits at $2/$10, but only until November 30, 2026, then doubles. [...] What is the best alternative to Kimi K3.1 Pro?

For most teams it is Claude Sonnet 5.5: the same $2 input and $10 output per million tokens, about three times the output speed on Artificial Analysis, and a slightly higher index score at max effort. If cost per finished task matters more than the sticker, test Claude Opus 5.5 at High effort, which Artificial Analysis measured at $1.82 per task against $2.11 for Kimi K3.1 Pro. The full Sonnet 5.5 review has the details.

Is there a cheaper alternative to Kimi K3.1 Pro? [...] What are the open-weight alternatives to Kimi K3.1 Pro?

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and MiMo-V2.6-Pro both ship MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face, and the older Kimi K3 has open weights under its own licence. Moonshot says the Kimi K3.1 Pro weights will be released by November 4, 2026, but they were not on Hugging Face when I checked. My MiMo V2.6 overview covers the Xiaomi option.

Is Claude Sonnet 5.5 better than Kimi K3.1 Pro?

At max effort Sonnet 5.5 scores 56.0 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against 55.1 for Kimi K3.1 Pro, at the same list price, and it outputs about 141 tokens per second against 50. Kimi is cheaper per finished task at max effort ($2.11 against $5.46), because Sonnet writes more tokens. My Kimi K3.1 Pro review and Sonnet 5.5 pricing posts go deeper.

results.title: 6 Best Kimi K3 Alternatives in 2026
results.content:
Kimi K3 is the largest open model yet shipped at 2.8 trillion parameters, and it is strong on agentic coding, reasoning, and multimodal work, but Moonshot admits a user-experience gap and the weights carry commercial license conditions rather than plain MIT.
   For polish and reliability, the closed-flagship alternatives are Claude Fable 5 for the most capable agent, GPT-5.6 Sol for the OpenAI ecosystem, Claude Opus 4.8 for reliability at a mid price, and Gemini 3.1 Pro for multimodal work on a smaller budget.
   For open weights on simpler terms, GLM-5.2 is MIT-licensed but text only, and DeepSeek V4 Pro is the cheapest option here.
   On raw token price, K3 at $3 input and $15 output per million undercuts Fable 5, Sol, and Opus 4.8, but not Gemini 3.1 Pro at its standard tier. [...] ### 4. Gemini 3.1 Pro

#### What it is

Gemini 3.1 Pro is Google's flagship Pro-tier model and the successor to the Gemini 3 Pro preview, though it still carries a preview label in Google's API docs, where it is listed as Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview.

Image 9: Google Gemini chat interface with model selector dropdown showing 3.5 Flash, 3.5 Thinking, and 3.1 Pro options, with 3.1 Pro selected

Pricing is context-tiered: $2 input and $12 output per million tokens up to 200K tokens, rising to $4 and $18 above that, per Google's pricing. It reads multiple modalities natively and carries one of the largest context windows on the market.

#### Strengths [...] For the most polished autonomous agent, Claude Fable 5 leads on user experience, with a premium price and an access history to plan around. Teams already on OpenAI get mature tooling from GPT-5.6 Sol, provided they watch the surcharge above 272K tokens. Claude Opus 4.8 is K3's true tier peer and the pragmatic pick for closed-model reliability at a fair price.

Gemini 3.1 Pro covers multimodal and long-context work on a smaller budget, as long as most requests stay under 200K tokens. GLM-5.2 gives an open-weight coding engine on unconditional MIT terms, without vision. DeepSeek V4 Pro is the cheapest open-weight route, at the cost of frontier-level reasoning.

results.content:
Not on a normal computer. It is a 2.8 trillion parameter mixture-of-experts model with 104 billion active parameters, so even an aggressive quantization needs hundreds of gigabytes of memory, a multi-GPU server rather than a desktop. The weights are due by November 4. A workable alternative is to use K3.1 Pro as the planner in Atomic Agent's Fusion mode with a local model doing the edits.

 How much does Kimi K3.1 Pro cost?  / /  

  On the Kimi API it costs $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million cached input tokens. The Highspeed variant has twice the input and output price. In our coding agent test one task cost about $0.16 to $0.21 at low reasoning effort and $0.35 to $0.46 at the default max effort. Claude Opus 5.5 cost $0.37 on the same task.
